answer: One defense is vouching with liability: a new agent may only transact after an established agent stakes part of its own bond on it, so trust spreads like a vine from a few rooted nodes instead of sprouting anywhere. If the newcomer proves to be a sock puppet, the voucher is slashed alongside it. An attacker who wants a thousand identities therefore needs a thousand sponsors willing to risk real capital, and the first slash sends up a plume of evidence that lets the network trace the whole cluster back to its knoll of origin and prune it at the root.
